d=pd.read_csv('spectrum.csv'); x=d.shift_cm1.values; y=d.intensity.values
# spike test: deviation of each point from mean of its two neighbours, relative to robust noise
dev=y[1:-1]-0.5*(y[:-2]+y[2:])
mad=np.median(np.abs(dev-np.median(dev)))*1.4826
z=(dev-np.median(dev))/mad
print('robust noise (neighbour-dev MAD)',round(mad/np.sqrt(1.5),1))
print('max |z|',round(np.abs(z).max(),2),'count |z|>6',int((np.abs(z)>6).sum()))
for i in np.argsort(-np.abs(z))[:5]: print(' ',x[i+1],y[i+1],round(z[i],1))
# full-range model: quadratic baseline + 4 Lorentzians (D, G, D', 2D) + D+G, fit 1100-3000
mod=PolynomialModel(degree=3,prefix='b_')
pars=mod.make_params(b_c0=200,b_c1=0,b_c2=0,b_c3=0)
comps=[(1344,2600,'D'),(1579,5300,'G'),(1623,400,'Dp'),(2690,15900,'2D'),(2940,300,'DG')]
for i,(c,a,_) in enumerate(comps):
    L=LorentzianModel(prefix=f'p{i}_')
    pars.update(L.make_params(**{f'p{i}_center':c,f'p{i}_amplitude':a*np.pi*12,f'p{i}_sigma':12}))
    pars[f'p{i}_sigma'].set(min=2,max=80)
    mod=mod+L
r=mod.fit(y,pars,x=x)
print('full fit redchi-free rms resid',round(r.residual.std(),1))
for i,(_,_,n) in enumerate(comps):
    c=r.params[f'p{i}_center']; s=r.params[f'p{i}_sigma']; a=r.params[f'p{i}_amplitude']
    print(f'{n:3s} center {c.value:8.2f}+/-{c.stderr or 0:5.2f} FWHM {2*s.value:6.2f}+/-{2*(s.stderr or 0):5.2f} height {a.value/(np.pi*s.value):8.0f}+/-{(a.stderr or 0)/(np.pi*s.value):6.0f}')
# residual by region
res=r.residual
for lo,hi in [(1100,1250),(1250,1450),(1450,1550),(1550,1700),(1700,2000),(2000,2550),(2550,2650),(2650,2800),(2800,3000)]:
    m=(x>=lo)&(x<hi); print(f' resid {lo}-{hi}: mean {res[m].mean():7.1f} std {res[m].std():6.1f}')

A monolayer 2D/G pattern with a weak D and D' is the standard sp2-carbon signature. The 2D single-Lorentzian form argues against multilayer graphene. No features of hBN, TMDs or amorphous carbon are present.

Same band set. Not excluded because the 2D FWHM of 32 cm-1 sits at the upper end of the monolayer range; bilayer 2D is expected to be multi-component and broader (order 50 cm-1), which is not seen in the single-Lorentzian fit (fit residual is at noise level in 2650-2800 cm-1). Discriminating this would need a multi-component 2D fit at higher S/N or a second spectrum.
Bulk graphite 2D band is broader and multi-component, and I2D/IG is typically well below the monolayer value. Rejected on the same 2D lineshape and ratio arguments.

Exclusion of TMDs and hBN relies on the absence of their characteristic bands in the window, not on their low-frequency modes.

One spectrum, no polarization series, no reference spectrum of the same substrate. Layer number is inferred from 2D lineshape and I2D/IG ratio. Absolute intensity is not used. A bilayer or few-layer contribution cannot be fully excluded from one fit.
2D FWHM of 32 cm-1 is at the upper end of monolayer values, so the layer call is probabilistic, not firm.

Strain and doping cannot be separated from one spectrum (G at 1579.3 cm-1 is a few cm-1 below the usual undoped monolayer value, which might hint at tensile strain or n-doping, but this is not decided here). A 2D-G correlation would be needed.

L_D = 6.3 nm uses the stage-1 relation of Cançado et al. (2011) at 532 nm, applied to I_D/I_G from peak heights. The calibration constant has a systematic uncertainty of order 10-20 % that the fit errors do not include. Area-based I_D/I_G (0.51) gives 6.2 nm.

D' is weak (height 405 ± 64 counts) and its width is poorly constrained (±3 cm-1). The defect-type classification from I_D/I_D' is therefore tentative, and the class ratios quoted from Eckmann et al. (2012) are from memory and were not checked in the paper text.

No measurement of the substrate-only background, so the SiO2 contribution to the baseline is unknown. The baseline was a cubic polynomial, and residuals are at the noise level (~135 counts) across the window, so this is not expected to bias the band parameters much.
No temperature or laser-power series, so heating cannot be checked. Stated temperature 295 K, laser 532 nm, no power given.
